title: Basement to Banner: Sonny's Ben Dover Goes 13-3 and Wins Buckaroo Bowl III
dek: Two years after back-to-back last-place finishes, Sonny rode a 13-3 season to the title, while Mekhi's Dawgs posted the year's biggest week and still ended up on the bottom rung of the ladder.
body: For two seasons, Ben Dover was where the Buckaroo Football League's standings went to end. In 2025, it was where they began. Sonny's team went 13-3, took the top seed, and beat The fumblers 105.1 to 86.48 in Buckaroo Bowl III, finishing a worst-to-first arc that would have sounded like fan fiction in December 2024. Kaushal's two-year hold on the trophy is over, and the guy who finished last twice now has a banner of his own.

The season started with the usual draft-day chaos, plus one entry that will live in league history: Mekhi drafted from basic training. That turned out to be a sign of how his year would go, with everything except the right timing. The real surprise of the early weeks, though, was what the league finally did after two straight trade-free seasons: it made four trades. After 28 weeks of nobody budging, four deals felt like a stock market boom.

The regular season was a scoring race that Sonny never actually led. Kaushal's Habibsters piled up 1,973.6 points, the most in the league by more than 115, and finished 8-8. Mekhi's Dawgs were second at 1,858.2, also 8-8. Ben Dover sat third in points at 1,850.8 and went 13-3 anyway, which is either brilliant lineup management, a magnificent run of schedule luck, or both. Whatever the formula, it worked every week that counted. Randy's The fumblers went 9-7 with 1,792.1 points and grabbed the second seed.

The year's strangest chapter belonged to Ramon. Araleasers had a rough start, including the lowest single week of the season, 61.4 in Week 3, and after Week 8 Ramon was removed from the league for inactivity. The team was renamed Ramon's Remains and played on without him, opening the new era with a 94.76 to 92.02 win over Alan in Week 9. Those results still count on Ramon's record, asterisk attached, which makes him the first manager in league history to win a game while not technically being in the league. The Remains finished 5-11 with 1,523.7 points and the fifth seed.

The playoffs opened with Randy's best performance of the year at the perfect moment. The fumblers hung 137.1 on Habibsters, who managed just 79.96, a 57.14-point beatdown that sent the league's highest-scoring team home and ended Kaushal's hopes of a three-peat. The Buckaroo Bowl was tighter but never really in doubt: Ben Dover scored 105.1, The fumblers answered with 86.48, and Sonny had his title by 18.62. Randy finished second, his best finish yet, and Kaushal settled for third.

Down the bracket, the consolation ladder delivered a twist even crueler than the standings. Alan's Team Pillbert entered as the sixth seed at 5-11 and climbed to fourth, while Ramon's Remains landed fifth. That left Mekhi's Dawgs, an 8-8 team with the second-most points in the league and the highest single week of the season, 153.62 in Week 9, finishing last. Two 5-11 teams finished ahead of him. Kai will have a hard time finding a box score that explains it, because there isn't one.

So the third page of the history book flips the first two. Sonny goes from the basement to the banner, Kaushal's dynasty takes its first loss, Randy reaches his first Bowl, and the league finally learned how to make a trade. Mekhi heads into the offseason with the biggest week of the year and the trophy nobody wants, and the league heads into 2026 with eight teams and a new question: is Ben Dover a one-year wonder, or the start of a new dynasty?
